record.title: Activity recognition from chest-worn accelerometers
record.abstract: Accurate activity recognition from chest-worn inertial measurement units is a prerequisite for context-aware physiological monitoring, yet most published benchmarks rely on wrist or hip placements. This study investigates the suitability of a single chest-mounted accelerometer for recognizing twelve daily-life activities including rest, walking, jogging, stair ascent and descent, cycling, and six sedentary postures. Features extracted in the time and frequency domains from three-axis acceleration signals were used to train and compare a k-nearest neighbor classifier, a random forest, and a support vector machine with radial basis function kernel. Data were collected from 45 healthy adults across a structured protocol lasting approximately 90 minutes per participant. The random forest achieved the highest overall accuracy of 92.3% in leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. A confusion analysis revealed that the chest location provides particularly strong discrimination between static postures, outperforming wrist placement on that sub-task. The findings support the integration of chest-worn accelerometers into ECG patch monitors for simultaneous cardiac and activity monitoring without additional sensor hardware.
